tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4411: money.Amount.Decimal() hardcoded 2 decimals (m/100, %02d), so CLP/JPY (0 decimals) and KWD (3 decimals) amounts and fees were misrendered in every API response and webhook payload. Decimal() now renders major units using the currency's own Exponent/Factor: integer for CLP/JPY ("15000"), 2 decimals for USD/EUR/etc. (unchanged, "10.50"), 3 for KWD ("1.234"), preserving the minus sign for negatives. Added money-level and API-level tests covering create/get/list rendering and fees for CLP, JPY, KWD and USD. go test -race, go vet and gofmt all pass.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4420: Service.Refund in payment/service.go validated a refund against the full payment amount (amount.Minor > p.Amount.Minor) instead of the remaining refundable balance, so cumulative refunds could exceed the payment (600+600 on 1000 → refunded 1200, remaining -200). The check now compares against p.Remaining() (Amount - already Refunded), rejecting excess refunds with ErrRefundExceedsRemaining (mapped by the API to 422 refund_exceeds_remaining) before any state change, while still allowing a refund of exactly the remaining amount which moves the payment to REFUNDED. Added regression test TestRefundExceedsRemainingAfterPartialRefund covering the ticket scenario: second over-remaining refund is rejected and leaves the payment untouched, exact-remaining refund succeeds and completes the refund. go test -race ./..., go vet and gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary:
Root cause: in store/memory.go ListByMerchant, the cursor already encodes `end` — the index one past the last item of the page (i.e. the first index of the next page) — but the decode path applied an extra `offset++`, skipping one payment at every page transition. With limit=50 over 1000 payments that dropped 19 payments (981 collected, none from the first page); with limit=1 it dropped every other payment.

Fix: removed the erroneous `offset++` so the decoded cursor is used directly as the resume offset, and updated the comment to document the cursor semantics. `next_cursor` is emitted only when `end < len(ids)`, so it is correctly empty on the last page, including when the total is an exact multiple of the limit.

Added regression test TestListWalkAllPages in store/memory_test.go: seeds 1000 payments and walks all pages with limits 1, 7, 50 and 100 (50/100 are exact divisors), asserting every payment is returned exactly once in creation order, non-last pages are full, and the walk terminates with an empty cursor after the expected number of pages.

Verified: go test -race ./... passes, go vet and gofmt are clean.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4450: the webhook retry predicate in webhook/dispatcher.go was inverted — `retryable` treated every 4xx (`status >= 400 && status < 500`) as transient and 5xx as permanent, exactly backwards from the README policy. Changed the condition to `status >= 500 && status < 600`, so transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx are retried with exponential backoff up to MaxAttempts, while other non-2xx statuses (400/401/404/410…) go straight to the dead-letter list after one attempt. The existing dead-letter path already records Attempts and LastStatus; added regression tests in webhook/webhook_test.go covering: permanent 4xx (400/401/404/410) dead-lettered after exactly 1 attempt with no backoff sleeps and correct Attempts/LastStatus, 503 retried to MaxAttempts (4) with 1s/2s/4s backoff then dead-lettered with Attempts=4/LastStatus=503, 5xx recovery on retry, and 408/429 retried. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass; no public API changes.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4461 in idempotency/store.go. Two bugs caused Idempotency-Keys to live 2×TTL: (1) Begin never checked whether an existing record was expired, so a key reused after the 24h TTL replayed the old cached response (or returned ErrKeyReuse/ErrInProgress); (2) purgeLocked evicted records only when now.Sub(ExpiresAt) > ttl, i.e. 48h after first use, explaining the two-day memory growth. Fixes: Begin now treats a record with now >= ExpiresAt as never used — it deletes the expired record and starts a brand-new request regardless of fingerprint (this per-record check also covers the once-per-minute purge throttle window); purgeLocked now evicts when now >= ExpiresAt, matching the documented "expired once now >= ExpiresAt" semantics. Pre-expiry replay/reuse/in-progress behavior and all public APIs are unchanged. Added regression tests: replay after TTL starts a new request, expired key ignores fingerprint, expired in-progress key restarts, exact boundary at first use + TTL (1ns before replays, at boundary starts new), and eviction of expired records from memory. go test -race ./..., go vet and gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4475: api/errors.go matched domain errors with a `switch err { case ... }` equality check, which stopped matching once errors were wrapped with context via fmt.Errorf("%w"). Rewrote errorResponse to match sentinels with errors.Is, restoring the documented mappings (404 not_found, 409 invalid_transition/conflict, 422 refund_exceeds_remaining, 400 invalid_request) while unexpected errors still return 500 with a generic message. Added TestDomainErrorMapping regression test covering the ticket scenarios. go build/vet/test -race/gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4488: Policy.Backoff used BaseDelay << (n-1) on int64, which overflowed to negative durations around attempt 35 with the enterprise policy (BaseDelay 1s, MaxAttempts 48), bypassing the MaxDelay cap and causing back-to-back retries. Rewrote Backoff as overflow-safe repeated doubling that returns MaxDelay before any doubling that would reach the cap, guaranteeing a positive, non-decreasing, capped wait for any attempt number. Added TestBackoffNeverOverflows regression test. go test -race ./..., go vet and gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
PAY-4510: added status filtering to the payment listing endpoint.

- payment.Page gained a `Status` field (zero value = no filter), an additive change that keeps the Repository interface and all constructors stable; updated the ListByMerchant contract docs.
- store.Memory.ListByMerchant now scans from the cursor offset skipping non-matching payments and collects one extra match to decide whether a next page exists. This keeps filtered pages full (exactly `limit` items) until the last match, preserves creation order, returns each match exactly once when walking next_cursor, and empties next_cursor after the last match. With no filter the behavior is identical to before (same items, same cursors).
- api.listPayments parses the optional `status` query parameter with the existing case-insensitive payment.ParseStatus; unknown values return 400 invalid_request via the standard error mapping.
- Added tests: store-level filtered walk (full pages, exactly-once, empty final cursor, no-match case) and API-level test (case-insensitive filter, creation order, paginated walk over the filtered view, other statuses, 400 invalid_request on unknown status).

go build, go vet, gofmt and go test -race ./... all pass.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary: Implemented PAY-4523: ops can re-deliver dead-lettered webhooks. Added webhook.ErrDeadLetterNotFound and Dispatcher.Replay(ctx, eventID) (bool, error), which removes the event from the dead-letter list and re-delivers it with the normal retry policy (same event id/payload, signature recomputed per attempt): (true, nil) on success, (false, nil) with the event re-dead-lettered exactly once on failure, and an ErrDeadLetterNotFound-wrapping error for unknown ids (restoring the entry if ctx aborts mid-delivery). Refactored the private deliver to report success (Flush unchanged). Exposed POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay returning 200 {"event_id","delivered"} and mapped ErrDeadLetterNotFound to 404 not_found. All tests (race), vet and gofmt pass.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
PAY-4530: added integer minor-unit amounts to the API, backward compatible.

- api/dto.go: createPaymentRequest/refundRequest gained `amount_minor` (*int64, so absent vs zero is distinguishable and non-integer JSON is rejected at decode); paymentResponse gained `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor`, `remaining_minor`; refundResponse gained `amount_minor`; toPaymentResponse populates them from the domain minor-unit integers, so every payment-returning endpoint (incl. list) carries them alongside the unchanged legacy fields.
- api/handlers.go: new resolveAmount helper used by createPayment and refundPayment (refunds resolve in the payment's currency). Exactly one of amount/amount_minor is required (neither -> 400 invalid_request); if both are present they must denote the same value, otherwise 400 invalid_request; amount_minor-only goes through money.New (validates currency), legacy amount keeps money.Parse.
- Idempotency: fingerprints are hashed from the resolved money.Amount (minor units + currency), so a retry using the other format for the same value hashes identically and is replayed — verified by test.
- Unknown JSON fields still rejected (DisallowUnknownFields unchanged).
- Added api/amount_minor_test.go covering all acceptance criteria (both endpoints, validation matrix, zero-exponent currencies, cross-format idempotent replay, list fields); README conventions updated. go build/vet/test -race and gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary: PAY-4541: Added payment.CanTransition(from, to Status) backed by a single allowedTransitions table (CREATED->PENDING/DECLINED, PENDING->SUCCEEDED/DECLINED, SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED) in payment/payment.go. Rewrote Service.Authorize, Capture, Decline and Refund to validate through CanTransition, removing all switch p.Status statements from payment/service.go. Refund is gated on the SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED edge so partial refunds are allowed exactly when full ones are. Pure refactor: identical errors (ErrInvalidTransition, ErrRefundExceedsRemaining, ...), events and return values; go build/vet/gofmt clean and go test -race ./... passes.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4555: made idempotency.Memory safe for concurrent use.

Root causes in idempotency/store.go:
1. Begin split its check-then-act across two lock acquisitions — two concurrent retries with the same key could both find no live record and both insert, each returning started=true (the duplicate refunds). It also read record fields (ExpiresAt, Fingerprint, Completed, Response) after unlocking, racing with Complete's writes.
2. Complete read the records map and mutated the record with no lock at all (the "no locking needed" comment was wrong) — concurrent with map writes in Begin/Release this caused the `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write` crashes and the -race reports.
3. Release did its existence check on the map outside the lock.

Fix: Begin, Complete and Release now hold m.mu for their entire critical section (single lock hold via defer). Begin's lookup/validate/insert is atomic, so per key exactly one concurrent Begin starts; others get ErrInProgress or, after Complete, a copy of the stored response (copied under the lock). Public API unchanged.

Added regression tests in idempotency/store_test.go: TestConcurrentBeginStartsOnce (64 goroutines, same key → exactly 1 start, rest ErrInProgress), TestConcurrentBeginReplayAfterComplete (retry loop → exactly 1 start, all others replay the stored 201 body), and TestConcurrentUse (16 goroutines hammering Begin/Complete/replay/Release/Len on the shared map). Verified: go build, go vet, gofmt clean, and `go test -race ./...` (plus -count=2 on the idempotency package) all pass.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
Root cause: store.Memory stored and returned payment.Payment values that shared the Refunds slice backing array with callers. Concurrent Service.Refund calls each received a Get copy aliasing the stored array, so their append() writes raced and overwrote each other; the loser of the optimistic-locking race failed Update with ErrVersionConflict but its refund had already landed in the shared array, which the winner's successful Update then persisted — producing the phantom refund id and a refunds list whose amounts don't add up to refunded_amount.

Fix (matching the fakeRepo convention already used in payment tests): clone at every repository boundary in store.Memory — Create stores p.Clone(), Get returns p.Clone(), Update stores p.Clone() with the version bump, and ListByMerchant returns clones. Optimistic-locking semantics (version check + increment) are unchanged, as are all public APIs. Also documented the "no shared mutable state across the boundary" contract on the payment.Repository interface.

Added regression tests in store/memory_test.go: TestNoSharedStateAcrossBoundary (mutating values passed to Create/Update or returned by Get/ListByMerchant never alters stored state), TestFailedUpdateLeavesNoTrace (a version-conflict update leaks nothing into the stored payment), and TestConcurrentRefundsConsistent (8 concurrent Service.Refund calls over Memory: race-free, stored refund sum equals refunded_amount, every stored refund id was returned to a client). Verified with go build, go vet, gofmt -l (clean) and go test -race ./... (all packages pass, including -count=2 on store and payment).

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
PAY-4570: Begin latency grew with traffic because every Begin call ran purgeLocked, which copied all records into a slice and sorted them by ExpiresAt — O(n log n) per request under the store mutex, so p99 grew with the number of live keys and only reset on pod restart.

Fix in idempotency/store.go:
1. Throttled eviction to at most once per minute (new purgeInterval const, tracked via a lastPurge field on Memory). Begin is now O(1) amortized regardless of how many keys are stored.
2. Simplified purgeLocked from sort-then-delete (O(n log n)) to a single O(n) map pass that deletes expired records.

Expiry semantics unchanged: Begin still checks now.Before(r.ExpiresAt) on the individual record before replaying, so expired keys are never replayed even between purges (verified by a new test with TTL < purge interval where no purge runs); expired records are still evicted by the periodic purge so memory stays bounded.

Added regression tests: TestExpiredKeyNotReplayedWithoutPurge, TestPurgeEvictsExpiredRecords, and BenchmarkBeginWithManyLiveKeys (50k live keys). Public API (NewMemory, Store interface) unchanged. go build, go vet, gofmt and go test -race ./... all pass.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4588: Fixed money.Allocate losing/creating cents in marketplace split payouts.

Root cause: Allocate computed each part independently as math.Round(float64 share), so rounded parts didn't sum to the charge (100.00/3 → 33.33×3 = 99.99; 0.05 split 1:1 → 0.03+0.03; 0.10 split 7 ways → 0.07). It also violated the repo's "money never touches floating point" convention.

Fix (money/allocate.go): reimplemented with the largest-remainder method in exact integer arithmetic, per the documented contract:
- each part gets floor(a.Minor*r/total), computed in 128 bits via math/bits.Mul64/Div64 so amount×ratio can never overflow;
- the leftover minor units (always fewer than the number of parts) are handed out one each to the parts with the largest fractional remainder, ties broken by lower index.
This guarantees the parts sum exactly to the charge and every part is within less than one minor unit of its exact share. Also hardened the ratio-sum validation to total <= 0 (catches int64 wraparound) with the same ErrInvalidAmount. Public API and error values unchanged.

Tests (money/money_test.go): added TestAllocateReconciles (the three ticket scenarios plus tie-breaking, zero-ratio, single-part, zero-amount cases), TestAllocateAlwaysSumsToAmount (property check: exact sum and <1-minor-unit deviation over many amounts/ratio sets), TestAllocateLargeValues (128-bit path, MaxInt64 amount), and extra error cases. go test -race ./..., go vet and gofmt all clean.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
PAY-4593: Retries with rebuilt JSON bodies were rejected with 422 idempotency_key_reused because the idempotency fingerprint hashed the raw request body bytes. The SDK's retry (`{"currency": "usd", "amount": "10.5", ...}` vs `{"merchant_id":"m_310","amount":"10.50","currency":"USD"}`) produced a different fingerprint for a semantically identical request.

Fix: fingerprint the parsed, normalized request instead of the raw bytes.
- api/idempotency.go: removed bodyFingerprint (raw-byte hashing); added fingerprint(parts ...string), which hashes the semantic fields of the request, each strconv.Quote'd so parts can't bleed into one another.
- api/handlers.go: createPayment now fingerprints (merchant_id, amount.String()) and refundPayment fingerprints (payment id, amount.String()), where the amount comes from money.Parse — so "10.5"/"10.50" both normalize to "10.50 USD" and "usd" to "USD". Key order and whitespace no longer matter since the raw body is never hashed.
- Semantically different requests reusing a key still get 422 (existing TestIdempotentCreateReplays covers this); in-progress/5xx storage semantics unchanged.
- Added regression tests TestIdempotentCreateReplaysRebuiltBody and TestIdempotentRefundReplaysRebuiltBody using the ticket's captured payloads, asserting the retry replays the original response (Idempotent-Replayed: true, identical body) and creates no duplicate payment/refund.

Verified: go build, go vet, gofmt clean, go test -race ./... all pass.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary: PAY-4601: money.Fee computed fees as math.Ceil(float64(minor)*float64(bps)/10000), which (a) always rounded up — overcharging one minor unit (10.05 USD @ 290 bps = 29.145 → charged 0.30 instead of 0.29) — and (b) lost exactness through float64 for large minor-unit amounts (KRW-like volumes, B2B invoices > 2^53). Rewrote Fee to follow the documented finance policy: exact integer computation with round half-to-even. The product minor*bps (up to ~9.2e22) overflows int64, so it is held as a 128-bit value via math/bits.Mul64 and divided by 10000 with bits.Div64 (provably no quotient overflow since the high word is < 10000); the remainder drives half-to-even rounding (up if > 1/2, ties to even). No floating point, consistent with the package's "money never touches floating point" rule; public API and error behavior unchanged. Added tests: the ticket example, half-to-even tie cases (0.5→0, 1.5→2, 2.5→2, 3.5→4), boundary neighbors, MaxInt64 and large-amount cases, plus a cross-check of many amount/bps combinations against an independent math/big half-even reference. go test -race ./..., go vet and gofmt all pass.
